claims.text: Replacing the EAM reference potential with an MTP trained on TaVCrW DFT data will reduce computational cost by more than 80%.
Replacing thermodynamic integration with free energy perturbation will maintain sub-meV free-energy accuracy.
The proposed accuracy depends on the MTP reproducing the ab initio phase-space distributions of both liquid and solid TaVCrW.
The MTP must reproduce the relevant phase-space distributions over 2000-2400 K.
The solid TaVCrW phase may exhibit short-range order.
Electronic excitations near the Fermi level affect the TaVCrW system.
The MTP can reproduce both configurational and vibrational components of the ab initio phase-space distribution in complex solid and liquid states.
The MTP can capture electronic-gap-related shifts.
Short-range order produces a stabilization energy of approximately 2-3 meV/atom.
FEP calculates free-energy differences directly when the MTP and ab initio phase-space distributions have sufficient overlap.
Using FEP with high-fidelity MTP sampling bypasses the slow convergence of thermodynamic integration.
The MTP captures nonlinear interactions, including magnetic fluctuations and short-range order, at a fraction of the DFT cost.
The proposed workflow will predict the melting temperature within 10 K of the TOR-TILD baseline.
The free-energy difference between the proposed and baseline methods will not exceed 0.5 meV/atom.
TOR-TILD using EAM potentials and thermodynamic integration is computationally expensive.
Empirical GGA-PBE/LDA underbinding and overbinding rules may fail for V and Cr.
A supercell containing more than 100 atoms is typically sufficient to resolve the short-range-order correlation length.
Restricting validation to 2000-2400 K ensures that electronic-gap effects and magnetic fluctuations remain within the MTP training distribution.
Violations of the V and Cr underbinding/overbinding rules at 0 K may propagate into high-temperature liquid predictions.
Neglecting high-temperature magnetic fluctuations in MTP training could cause free-energy errors greater than 0.5 meV/atom.

contradictions.description: The mechanism states that the MTP captures magnetic fluctuations, whereas the uncertainty field says high-temperature magnetic fluctuations may be neglected in the MTP training data.

The hypothesis describes 'sub-meV accuracy in melting temperature prediction,' which mixes an energy unit with a temperature prediction; the predicted-outcome field separately specifies a 10 K melting-temperature tolerance and a 0.5 meV/atom free-energy tolerance.
